title: Move per-environment ifs into application-{profile}.yml and @Profile
summary: The prod and staging branches in NotificationService move into config files and a bean switch, and then staging wants real mail too.

turns.user: NotificationService keeps growing ifs on app.env. the only things that differ per env are the url and whether mail actually goes out

assistant.body: Great, that splits cleanly into two kinds. A value that differs, like the URL, goes into application-{profile}.yml and Spring picks the file. Behaviour that differs, sending real mail or only logging it, becomes two Mailer implementations with @Profile deciding which one is a bean. NotificationService no longer knows which environment it runs in, which is a nice separation of concerns.

# application.yml
app:
  base-url: http://localhost:8080

# application-staging.yml
app:
  base-url: https://staging.shop.example.com

# application-prod.yml
app:
  base-url: https://shop.example.com

turns.user: nice. oh wait, staging should send real smtp too, QA wants to see the actual mails. also how do i pick the profile when starting it

assistant.body: Besides ! a @Profile also takes & and |. SmtpMailer becomes active on prod and staging, and LoggingMailer only when it is neither. Note: in the replacement side of sed a bare & stands for the whole match, so it is escaped as \&. The profile is passed with --spring.profiles.active at startup, or through the SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE environment variable.
